title: Élision
subtitle: Dropping the final vowel before a word beginning with a vowel or mute h. The apostrophe as notation.
objectives: Understand élision as the deletion of a final vowel before an initial vowel.
Recognize which words undergo élision: le, la, je, me, te, se, ce, de, ne, que.
Apply élision correctly in writing with the apostrophe.
Distinguish between élision (vowel drops) and liaison (consonant links).

sections.heading: What élision is
sections.body:
Élision is the deletion of a final vowel before a word that starts with a vowel or silent h. The dropped vowel is replaced by an apostrophe in writing.

- le + ami = l'ami
- la + école = l'école
- je + ai = j'ai
- ne + est = n'est

The apostrophe marks the absence, not the presence. It says: a vowel was here, but I dropped it to avoid a hiatus.

sections.heading: Which words undergo élision
sections.body:
Only a small set of words undergo élision. They are all single-syllable function words:

- Articles: le, la → l'
- Pronouns: je, me, te, se, ce → j', m', t', s', c'
- Prepositions: de → d'
- Conjunctions: que → qu'
- Negation: ne → n'

The plural article 'les' does not elide; it makes liaison instead: les amis, not l'amis.

The masculine article 'le' elides before vowels: l'homme. The feminine 'la' also elides: l'école. This means that 'l'' is ambiguous — you cannot tell from the form alone whether the noun is masculine or feminine. The full form must be learned.

sections.heading: Élision and the aspirated h
sections.body:
Élision, like liaison, is blocked by an aspirated h. You write 'le héros', not 'l'héros'. The apostrophe never appears before an aspirated h.

This is the same rule as liaison: aspirated h creates a word boundary. Silent h does not.

sections.heading: Élision versus liaison
sections.body:
Do not confuse them.

- Élision drops a vowel: le + homme = l'homme.
- Liaison links a consonant: les + hommes = [lezɔm].

Both apply before vowels. Some words do both, in sequence: de + les + hommes = des hommes, with liaison [dezɔm].

items.prompt: Can you elide before an aspirated h?
items.answer: No. Élision is blocked by aspirated h. Ex: le héros, not l'héros.

items.prompt: Which of these words undergo élision: le, les, un, de, ne?
items.answer: le, de, ne. Not les or un.
